# vaultwarden_organization_group (Resource)

This resource creates a group in a Vaultwarden organization.

Groups require the `ORG_GROUPS_ENABLED=true` setting on the Vaultwarden server. Updates keep the group's members and collection access, including ones managed outside Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "vaultwarden_organization" "example" {
  name = "Example"
}

resource "vaultwarden_organization_group" "example" {
  organization_id = vaultwarden_organization.example.id
  name            = "Engineering"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the group
- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization that the group belongs to

### Optional

- `access_all` (Boolean) Whether the members of the group have access to all collections of the organization. Defaults to `false`. Vaultwarden 1.37 and later do not return this value, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected on those versions
- `external_id` (String) An identifier to link the group to an external system, such as a directory service. Vaultwarden cannot change the external ID of an existing group, so changing it replaces the group

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the group

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import vaultwarden_organization_group.example <org_id>/<group_id>
```
